title: Zero a robot arm's elbow: hold its forearm level at the zero marks while the other hand pushes in the zeroing pin
instruction: Zero the robot arm's elbow: take the zeroing pin out of its holder; with one hand lift the robot's hanging forearm until the two yellow zero marks on top of the elbow line up and hold it there, while the other hand pushes the pin into the zeroing hole on the front of the elbow until it is home and the elbow's green light comes on; then let go of the forearm and the pin, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Robot technicians zero (master) a robot's joints after a motor or encoder change: with the joint's brake released they hold the link at its zero marks and lock it there with a pin, so the controller can record the zero. The released link drops under its own weight, so one hand holds it while the other fits the pin.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A small six-axis robot arm of orange-painted aluminium with grey joints, fixed: its black base plate (12.4 cm across) on the table 32 cm forward and 24 cm left of the centre line, a shoulder 7.5 cm up, and an upper arm reaching right to the elbow, whose axis runs forward 32 cm out, 8 cm left of the centre line and 11.5 cm above the table. The elbow housing has two orange cheeks 7.4 cm across either side of the forearm's grey hub; on the front cheek's face, 2.2 cm left of the axis, is the zeroing hole (0.8 cm across, in a steel bush). Yellow zero marks sit on top of both cheeks and of the hub, and a status light (dark; green once zeroed) on top of the elbow housing. (2) The forearm (0.30 kg, orange, 3.4 cm wide and 3.6 cm deep), reaching 18.8 cm right from the elbow's axis to a grey wrist and a black tool flange; its brake is released, so it hangs 30 degrees below level on its stop. (3) The zeroing pin (0.08 kg): a steel shaft 0.8 cm thick and 4 cm long with a red plastic handle 3 cm long, 1.4 cm wide and 3.4 cm tall, lying in its holder (a grooved aluminium block, fixed) pointing forward, its handle 20.5 cm forward and 16.5 cm left of the centre line. (4) The robot's teach pendant (dark grey, with a screen and a red emergency stop) lying on the table 43 cm forward and 17 cm right of the centre line, fixed (scenery). The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The forearm's angle is measured below level about the elbow's axis; the zero marks line up within 4 degrees of level. The pin is in the zeroing hole once its tip has entered the hole (within 6 mm of its axis, tilted less than 12 degrees); it then slides along the hole. It passes through the front cheek (1.1 cm) at any angle, but goes on into the hub only while the marks are lined up; otherwise its tip stops against the hub. Pushed 1.6 cm deep with the marks lined up, the pin is home: the elbow is pinned at its zero, the pin holds the forearm level and the green light comes on. At the end: 1.0 with the elbow pinned at its zero and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.5 with the elbow pinned at its zero; 0.25 with the pin in the zeroing hole; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the forearm and the pin still.
reset_notes: Draw the pin out and lay it back in its holder pointing forward; let the forearm down onto its stop.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: a scaled-down robot (40 cm long) built from boxes and cylinders, fixed except the forearm, which turns on a free hinge with a stop 30 degrees below level. The pin slides in the hole on a joint switched on as it enters; the task file stops it at the hub unless the forearm is within 4 degrees of level, and once it is home a fixed joint holds the forearm level. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
